children.text: Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity, Inc. was founded on January 9, 1914, at Howard University in Washington, D.C.
Our motto: Culture For Service and Service For Humanity.

From its founding at Howard University, Phi Beta Sigma has placed service at the center of fraternity life. In Woodstock, Sigma Delta Sigma carries that tradition into its education, business and social action programs.
Phi Beta Sigma was founded by A. Langston Taylor, Leonard F. Morse, and Charles I. Brown.
The three founders established Phi Beta Sigma at Howard University in Washington, D.C., on January 9, 1914. The fraternity’s principles are brotherhood, scholarship and service.
“Woodstock, GA is our base of operation, but we are dedicated to providing services in the name of Sigma where we are needed.” — Sam Mitchell, from the chapter’s welcome message

Nineteen brothers came together to charter Sigma Delta Sigma in Woodstock, Georgia. On May 6, 2019, the International General Board granted their charter. Today the chapter invites neighbors across Cherokee and Cobb counties to take part in its work.

title: Bigger & Better Business

children.text: Phi Beta Sigma first introduced Bigger and Better Business at its Tenth Anniversary Conclave in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in December 1924. It became the fraternity's first national program.

From the outset, the program promoted Black-owned businesses. It encouraged owners to sharpen their business skills, run their businesses more efficiently and improve service to the public so they could compete more effectively.
Brother Hill is exploring ways to bring three international initiatives to our chapter.
Project S.E.E.D.
Sigma Business Initiatives
Tax Awareness

summary: Phi Beta Sigma's first national program champions Black-owned businesses. Today, Sigma Delta Sigma is exploring programs in entrepreneurship and tax awareness.

title: Education

children.text: Phi Beta Sigma has long regarded education and academic achievement as foundations for success. At the 1945 Conclave in St. Louis, Missouri, the fraternity reorganized its programs and established Education as an international program.

The program serves alumni and collegiate members and helps them support students in their communities. At the local, regional and national levels, its work includes scholarships, conferences, college fairs, mentoring and tutoring.
International initiatives
Adopt-A-School
Sigma members work with teachers and principals in local schools to help students build literacy, strengthen academic skills and deepen their understanding of what they study.
Scholarships
Phi Beta Sigma awards scholarships to high school and college students to help cover the cost of their education.
Scholarships in our chapter

The chapter recognizes students through the Anna James Academic Scholarship and the Bishop Stephen Hall Sr. Scholarship. In 2025, Emily Jemison and Molly Lin were recognized in the Anna James program, and Donovan J. Sutton received the Bishop Stephen Hall Sr. award. Contact the chapter to ask about the next scholarship cycle or discuss a partnership with your school.

summary: Phi Beta Sigma supports students through school partnerships and scholarships. In our chapter, the Anna James Academic Scholarship and the Bishop Stephen Hall Sr. Scholarship recognize academic achievement.

title: Social Action

children.text: Bro. Elmo M. Anderson conceived the Social Action program in 1934 to improve the well-being of disenfranchised people.
The International Social Action Program encourages social, political and philanthropic leadership to strengthen our communities and our membership. We pursue that mission in five ways.
Educate fraternity members about health issues that affect them and their families.
Help members build a sense of self-worth and become more visible in their communities through service.
Provide information about political and community issues and help members understand the legislative process.
Involve members in raising funds for organizations that share our vision.
Promote health awareness so members and their families can prevent illness and maintain their health.

summary: Through Social Action, Sigma Delta Sigma brings neighbors together for community service, health education and civic engagement in Cherokee and Cobb counties.
